title: Dalfampridine in WWOX-LoF
summary: An acute probe of callosal propagation and recruitment.

graph.evidence: A genetic mouse model had shorter callosal peak latency during acute exposure.
graph.inference: A compound peak can change when the mixture of conducting fibers changes.
graph.hypothesis: Surviving WWOX axons may have acutely recoverable propagation reserve.
graph.experiment: Measure distal failures of the same component at matched proximal recruitment.

evidence: In Gtf2i-deficient mice, 4-aminopyridine shortened callosal peak latency in mutants and controls. In adult brain injury, some structural markers improved while conduction velocity did not show recovery after washout.
inference: The synthetic replay increased apparent compound-peak speed from 0.49 to 0.82 m/s by changing fiber weights while leaving both fiber speeds fixed.
hypothesis: An acute action could recover transmission in surviving WWOX axons. Recruitment of a different fiber mixture or a larger synaptic response can produce an apparent gain.
experiment: At verified local exposure, track direct components across distance and compare distal train failures at matched proximal recruitment. Record later synaptic responses and spontaneous activity separately.
limits: Retain as a conditional ex vivo probe. Free juvenile neural exposure is unmeasured. The US label contraindicates dalfampridine in people with a seizure history.
